answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because island only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, vine is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any pearl approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
